subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin hot-reload without container restart (jiti cache invalidation)

question: Should OpenClaw support live plugin source/install reload as a first-class Gateway/CLI lifecycle, or keep plugin development restart-only with better diagnostics and docs?
rationale: The useful fix crosses plugin loader caches, runtime teardown, registry replacement, Gateway reload semantics, CLI/RPC UX, and documentation; repository policy currently treats plugin metadata as process-stable unless an owner-defined reload flow exists.

options.title: Design first-class reload
options.body: Specify and implement a Gateway-owned reload operation that safely disposes old plugin state, invalidates loader caches, replaces runtime registries, and exposes a documented CLI/RPC entrypoint.

options.title: Keep restart-only
options.body: Leave source/install changes restart-backed and improve docs/logging so users know when a full Gateway restart is required and how to verify the active runtime.

options.title: Add cache diagnostics only
options.body: Expose a narrow cache diagnostic or clear command without live registry replacement, accepting that users still need a restart for safe activation.

recommendation.title: Design first-class reload
recommendation.body: Specify and implement a Gateway-owned reload operation that safely disposes old plugin state, invalidates loader caches, replaces runtime registries, and exposes a documented CLI/RPC entrypoint.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the keep-open product/design note and has recent Gateway reload pipeline history.
